scenes.question: Where is the biggest jump in the record?

beats.say: Imagine a long staircase in the dark. You walk along it with your hand on the wall, feeling for the one place where the floor suddenly steps up. If there is one big step, you will find it. If the floor is smooth, you will find nothing.

Formula thirty-three, the Pettitt change-point test, scans every possible split year for the single most likely jump. On the raw stitched record it should find the 2012 instrument seam. On the harmonised record, it should not.

scenes.title: The seam Pettitt should find
scenes.subtitle: October + November fire cell-days · Punjab and Haryana · FIREWORK archive calendar

beats.say: Here is the raw stitched record: MODIS before 2012, VIIRS from 2012. The step is impossible to miss.
That step is the instrument, not the fields. A good harmonisation should make it disappear, and Pettitt gives us a direct before-and-after check.

parts.say: For a candidate split at year t, U t compares every year before the split, i, with every year after it, j.
Each comparison gives plus one if the later year is higher, minus one if lower. If everything after the split is higher, U t becomes very large.
K is the biggest size of U t over all possible splits. The year where it peaks is the most likely change point.
And this turns K into an approximate p-value, given n years. A big K means a small p: a jump that chance alone is unlikely to make.

steps.label: Raw stitched · K
steps.say: On the raw stitched series, K is 122, with the change after 2011 and a p-value of 0.0082. That is the instrument seam at 2012, found exactly.

steps.label: Harmonised · K
steps.say: On the harmonised series, K drops to 76, and the most likely split moves to after 2017.

steps.label: Harmonised · p-value
steps.say: Its p-value is 0.24, not significant. The seam is gone. The weak split that remains marks the start of the recent decline. But a non-significant result is necessary, not sufficient, because the test has low power with 25 points.

beats.say: This figure shows the Pettitt statistic U t for every split year. The black line is the raw stitched series, and it peaks sharply at the 2012 seam.
The violet line is the harmonised series. Its peak is much lower, and no longer at the instrument change.

beats.label: Gates summary
beats.say: On the FIREWORK website, open the Validation page. Pettitt is one of the checks that the seam is really gone. FIREWORK pairs it with placebo years and the seam ratio of formula thirty-five, because one weak test is not enough.

points: Scan every split year; K = largest |U_t|
Harmonised: p = 0.24, the seam is gone

beats.say: So, to remember: Pettitt finds the single biggest step. It finds the 2012 seam in the raw record, and does not find it after harmonisation.
Next, formula thirty-four: PELT, multiple change points.
